item.title: Local Patients Among 1,500 Waiting Over an Hour for Ambulances
item.description: It's emerged that patients locally were among fifteen-hundred that waited more than an hour for an ambulance in the first half of this year. According to National Ambulance Service figures, 365 of these delayed responses occurred in the region covering Leitrim and Roscommon. Earlier this year, 52-year-old Drumshanbo resident had to wait an hour and twenty minutes for an ambulance to arrive after having suffered from a stroke. item.title: 24 New Speed Camera Zones Aim to Curb Local Speeding
item.description: It's hoped that the introduction of 24 new speed camera zones will see a crackdown on speeding locally. Gardaí announced the new measures yesterday, with 15 to be allocated in Roscommon. There will be six in Leitrim, while Longford will have three with one more community request, Advertisement The primary purpose of safety cameras is to reduce speed-related collisions, lessen injuries and save lives on Irish roads. item.title: Gardaí to conduct checkpoints on roads as part of Christmas safety campaign
item.description: Gardaí will continue to have an increased presence on the roads today, as part of their Christmas safety campaign. They say the festive period is one of the most dangerous times of year for road users, with too many lives still being lost and serious injuries occurring in preventable collisions. Over three thousand checkpoints have been carried out so far this month, and hundreds of people have been arrested for drink or drug driving. item.description: Hundreds of people will take part in charity walks and runs in the Shannonside region today and tomorrow. Many events are taking place in the region over the next few days also. item.title: Baptists to celebrate first Christmas in new Carrick chapel
item.description: The Baptist Church will celebrate Christmas Day in their new chapel in Carrick-on-Shannon for the first time today. They moved into the former Crumbs restaurant on Bridge Street earlier this month. The building was converted into a church after it was given the green light by Leitrim County Council. item.title: Roscommon woman encouraging people to visit art exhibition
item.description: A Roscommon woman is encouraging people to try something different this Christmas and visit an art exhibition. Curraghboy native Avril Egan is among those whose work features at The Village at Burgess in Athlone. The group exhibition opened in the run up to Christmas and will continue until the end of January. item.title: 'Recommit to presence of God in our lives' - Bishop Paul Connell's Christmas message
item.description: The Bishop of Ardagh and Clonmacnoise is encouraging people to recommit to the presence of God in their lives this Christmas. Paul Connell says God is with us throughout our fears, pains, joys and sorrows. He says he's our dependable friend, who is with us in everyday events in our daily lives. item.description: The Bishop of Achonry and Elphin is expressing solidarity with refugees this Christmas. Kevin Doran says, when migrants come here, they often bring gifts that benefit our society. He made the comments in his Christmas message, which we can hear in full now: Advertisement

item.title: Annual tractor run in memory of popular Arigna man to take place tomorrow
item.description: An annual tractor run in memory of a popular local man will take place in Arigna tomorrow. Registration for the James Cull Memorial Tractor Run starts at 11 o'clock at Drumshanbo Mart. The event has raised thousands of euro for the mental health charity North West Stop in recent years. James Cull died by suicide at the age of 20 in 2019, just five years after his father Oweney had taken his own life. item.title: Annual fundraiser for Western Alzheimers to take place in Roscommon
item.description: The annual fundraising walk for Western Alzheimers Roscommon branch takes place tomorrow. It starts at 12 Noon from Hannon's Hotel in Roscommon town and features both 5 and 10K routes. Walkers, runners, buggys and pets are invited to take part on the day. Entry is a €10 donation per person and €20 for families. Chairperson of Western Alzheimers voluntary branch, Mairead Nally, is hoping for good weather: Advertisement
